stories.title: Castlebar braced for monumental Mayo homecoming
stories.summary: Mayo will likely have to upscale plans for the homecoming of their triumphant footballers this evening as the county prepares for an enormous celebration in Castlebar. The green and red ended a 75-year wait for the Sam Maguire Cup on Sunday when they defeated Kerry at Croke Park to spark a monumental outpouring of joy in the stands. Thousands will attend a special homecoming event at Hastings Insurance McHale Park, with the team expected to arrive at around 6pm. Work began on a potential homecoming in the immediate aftermath of Mayo's semi-final victory over Louth three weeks ago.

stories.title: France braces for fresh heatwave as fires rage on
stories.summary: Shelters in France and Spain overflowed today with exhausted locals and holidaymakers forced to flee blazes so massive some were forming their own mini weather systems, as authorities warned a new heatwave was set to descend on parts of the region. The fires tearing through forests in southwest France, around the prized wine-making region of Bordeaux, and in central Spain, around the capital Madrid, have been some of the worst in decades and have hit at the height of the summer holiday season. More than 325,000 people have fled their homes in the face of the blazes feeding on forests left super-dry by successive heatwaves and lack of rain since May. "Everyone had to get out of the village quickly - it was a critical situation and people were scared," Olga Congacha, 50, told AFP on a highway in the Madrid region, where police had closed off access to her home, Robledo de Chavela.

stories.title: Three dead after shooting at Seattle food festival
stories.summary: Three people have been killed and at least four others wounded, including a toddler, after an apparent gunfight near the Space Needle landmark in Seattle last night, according to police. Seattle Police said one suspect had been arrested and they were searching for another following the incident at the Bite of Seattle food festival in a popular tourist district of the northwestern US city. Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis said shots were heard around 6pm (2am Irish time) and "there were two people who we believe were shooting at each other." Two weapons were recovered. Police said on X earlier Sunday there were "multiple shooting victims" after shots were fired at the Seattle Center.

stories.title: Phoenix Park reopens historic Magazine Fort to the public
stories.summary: The Office of Public Works will officially reopen the Magazine Fort in Phoenix Park today. The historic site, designed by military engineer John Corneille, was built between 1734 and 1736 as a military storage facility. Ammunition and gunpowder, which had previously been stored in Dublin Castle, were moved to the fort after it was deemed a safer location outside the city. The fort later played a significant role in the Easter Rising, when it was raided on Easter Monday, 24 April 1916.

stories.title: Brazil recalls ambassador to Argentina over Milei speech
stories.summary: Brazil has recalled its ambassador to Argentina for consultations following "insults" levelled by President Javier Milei against his Brazilian counterpart Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. The comments were made by Mr Milei at a Sao Paulo political event, the foreign ministry said. The libertarian leader of Argentina referred to Brazil's leftist incumbent president as a "convict" and a "thief", without naming him explicitly, during an event on Saturday formally nominating right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro to run in upcoming elections. Mr Milei also referred to - without naming him directly - Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes as "bald trash."

stories.title: 'Consumed by hate' - Infantino hits back at critics
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has hit back at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives while defending the tournament as a success that celebrated unity, safety and inclusion. In an open letter published on Monday, Infantino, 56, said detractors had overlooked the joy and togetherness experienced by millions of fans around the world who witnessed the tournament, won by Spain and staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico. "You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all," he said. "To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best ‌show in the world.

stories.title: Off-duty garda killed in single-vehicle crash in Co Clare
stories.summary: An off-duty garda was killed in a single-vehicle car crash in Co Clare yesterday evening. The collision happened shortly after 5.30pm yesterday on the R466 outside the village of Broadford. Gardaí and emergency services attended the scene, where the passenger of the car, was pronounced dead. The garda, a man in his 50s, was based at a station in Limerick city.

stories.title: Ukraine air barrage kills two, wounds 17 in Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine fired hundreds of drones at Russia early today, killing two people and setting multiple buildings ablaze, according to Russian officials. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said his forces had struck an export terminal in the western Rostov region, as well as oil facilities in the Yaroslavl and Udmurtia regions far from from the front line. "Last night, our long-range sanctions were effective in the Rostov region. An export terminal approximately 250 kilometres (155 miles) from the front line was hit," Zelensky said in a post on Facebook. "Deep strikes also targeted oil facilities in the Yaroslavl region and the Udmurt Republic, which is 1,300 kilometres from Ukraine's state border," he added.

stories.title: Oil prices drop as US, Iran pause fighting over weekend
stories.summary: Oil prices tumbled more than 5% today after the US and Iran paused strikes over the weekend after two weeks of attacks, raising hopes of a diplomatic solution that would de-escalate the conflict and allow shipping to resume in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures fell $5.70, or around 5.9%, to $91.08 a barrel this morning after briefly slipping under the key support level of $90 earlier in the session. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $84.51 a barrel, down $4.80, or around 5.4%. Both contracts are trading at their lowest levels in nearly a week after rising for the past three weeks.

stories.title: Burnham to host Zelensky in first foreign leader visit
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will host Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as his first foreign leader since taking office a week ago. The pair were set to visit a British naval base and hear from both countries' armed forces personnel involved in training Ukrainian service members for battle, Burnham's Downing Street office announced yesterday evening. It said he would vow "to continue the unbreakable bond between the two nations", echoing what the new UK leader told Mr Zelensky in a call last Monday within hours of replacing Keir Starmer. "Britain stands with Ukraine, shoulder to shoulder, and our support remains unwavering," Mr Burnham said in a statement.

stories.title: Red Sea traffic slows after Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb has fallen after Yemeni Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast. Transit through the Strait of Hormuz stayed low over the weekend, shipping data from Kpler showed on Monday. Eleven commodity vessels passed through the Bab el-Mandeb strait yesterday, the lowest level in months, the data showed. Red Sea traffic has been disrupted off the coast of Yemen since last week by the Tehran-aligned Houthis, who want to blockade Saudi exports, expanding the US-Iran conflict that has already choked oil supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.summary: Gardaí are treating as suspicious the discovery of the body of a homeless man in west Dublin two days ago. The body of 35-year-old Andrew Haire was discovered at a recycling centre last Friday. He had been moving between Cork, Kilkenny and Dublin in the week before he died. Gardaí have deployed the resources of a criminal investigation and issued an appeal for information.

stories.title: 'Enjoy every minute' - Biden among tributes to Mayo
stories.summary: Former US president Joe Biden has paid tribute to the Mayo team after their historic All-Ireland win yesterday. Yesterday, the Green and Red put 75 years of hurt behind them as they beat Kerry 1-20 to 1-17 at Croke Park. After more than seven decades of hope and heartbreak, a dream held for generations came true. In Castlebar and in towns across the county last night, crowds gathered to celebrate a fourth All Ireland title and a first since 1951.

stories.title: O'Donoghue man of the match and TSG player of the season
stories.summary: No tomorrow, no yesterday, just the here and now and the afterglow of Mayo's magnificent achievement in ending a 75-year famine to become All-Ireland Senior Football Champions again. How they suffered down the years; now they can host the mother of all parties in the erstwhile named House of Pain. No one deserves it more. It will hardly come as any surprise that Ryan O'Donoghue has been named as the All-Ireland final man of the match and The Sunday Game player of the season. The commentators on Midwest Radio, in the throes of delirium as they called the magic moments following the final whistle of their 1-20 to 1-17 win over Kerry, declared it a done deal. Who could argue.

stories.title: Man dies in Clare crash as three killed over 24 hours
stories.summary: Gardaí are appealing for witnesses following a road crash in Co Clare in which a man in his 50s died. The collision happened shortly after 5.30pm Saturday on the R466 at Gortnaglogh, Broadford. Gardaí and emergency services attended the scene, where the passenger of the car, a man in his 50s, was pronounced dead. The driver, who is also aged in his 50s, was airlifted to University Hospital Limerick with serious injuries.

stories.title: Mayo's House of Pain comes to an end as they stun Kerry
stories.summary: The House of Pain has closed its doors. It's an historic relic now. Mayo people might even go visit it from time to time. Those two own goals? Donie Vaughan’s red card? Early goal after early goal? Yeah, they still hurt, but they don’t hurt just as much anymore. Jordan Flynn’s slap against the crossbar late on in Sunday's 1-20 to 1-17 win over Kerry? Finally, the footballing Gods said 'no, that’s enough now.’ When the Crossmolina man missed the chance to seal this All-Ireland with 63:12 on the clock, a score that would have put Mayo eight clear and cruising, an uneasy silence engulfed most of the stadium.

stories.title: Suspect in Berlin Pride attack shot and killed - police
stories.summary: The chief suspect in a deadly attack near Berlin's Pride parade has been shot dead, police said this evening. Officers located the suspect, previously named as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, at around 6pm local time, Berlin police said in a statement on social media. "Around 6 p.m. (1600 GMT), the suspect involved in yesterday's attack in Tiergarten was located at an allotment garden complex in Spandau," Berlin police wrote on X. "According to initial findings, he ran towards officers while armed with a bladed weapon; police... subsequently opened fire. Despite immediate ‌resuscitation efforts by the Berlin Fire Department, he died at the scene."

stories.title: 'Historic situation' in France, Spain sees new fire front
stories.summary: Fire crews in France and Spain battling unchecked wildfires that have forced more than 300,000 people to flee were overwhelmed as the unpredictable blazes advanced. France's southwestern city of Bordeaux, at the heart of a region of vineyards, was under threat, with a major highway and train lines cut. In Spain more villages in the fire zone raging west of Madrid were emptied during the night -- and a new front opened near the coastal city of Valencia. France was faced with "a historic situation", Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said late last night.

stories.title: Pilots become first mother and daughter to fly together
stories.summary: Two Aer Lingus pilots made history earlier this week after becoming the first mother and daughter to operate a commercial flight together for the airline. Captain Sonya Bissett from Malahide in Dublin, who has been a commercial pilot with Aer Lingus for over 27 years, was joined on flight EI 650 from Dublin to Frankfurt by her daughter, First Officer Lara Danaher. While there have been many previous examples of family members working together on an Aer Lingus flight, it is the first time a mother and daughter operated a flight together in a proud moment for both Ms Bissett and Ms Danaher. "I remember when Lara was about four years of age, she always knew two pilots 'flew the plane'. When I was putting on my uniform for work one day she said, 'I know what mum, when I grow up, I’ll be a pilot, that way I can come to work with you and we can fly the plane together'," she said.

stories.title: Man charged after girl injured in Tyrone quad bike crash
stories.summary: A man has been charged after an eight-year-old girl and a man were seriously injured in a collision in Co Tyrone. The crash involved a van and a quad bike on the Edergole Road in Omagh before 7.05pm yesterday. Chief Inspector McConville said the driver of the Peugeot Partner van, a 26-year-old man, was arrested on suspicion of a number of offences. Police said a 26-year-old man had been charged with driving with excess alcohol in breath, two counts of causing grievous bodily injury by dangerous driving, and a number of other related offences.
